newsitem.title: FINLAND: RECORD VOLUMES SEEN IN FINNISH BOND AUCTION.
newsitem.headline: RECORD VOLUMES SEEN IN FINNISH BOND AUCTION.

text.p: Analysts expect record volumes in the Finnish State Treasury's auction of five- and 10-year benchmark bonds on Thursday, as substantial new liquidity is due to pour onto the market.

"There is approximately 17 billion markka of liquidity coming into the market soon ... the auction is an almost guaranteed success from the issuer's point of view," said OKOBANK treasury economist Teijo Rantatupa.
September 15 is the maturity date for the old 1996 benchmark which carries a 6.50 percent coupon and amounts to roughly 16 billion markka in capital payments and accrued interest.
Coupon payments are also due on that date for the 2001 benchmark (10.00 percent coupon) and a housing bond, which will add 2.6 billion markka in total.
The bonds to be auctioned on Thursday September 12 are due to be paid on September 16, one day after the tide of liquidity hits the market, analysts noted.
The biggest amount raised for one Finnish bond at auction so far is 3.8 billion markka, in 1993. The largest bid ever received for one bond was 6.19 billion markka in July, for the 2001 benchmark.
Analysts forecast Thursday's total auction volume in a 4-7 billion markka range with particularly the longest benchmark 7.25 percent bond due 2006 attracting interest, including from overseas.
"The 2006 bond still provides potential," said Jukka Lepomaki, chief analyst at Merita Bank.
"There are clear signs that (overseas investors) are seeking spreads that yield over Germany," he added.
The previous 2006 auction raised 2.46 billion markka at 99.70 and a yield of 7.29 percent. The current outstanding amount in the bond is 10.42 billion markka.
But five-year 2001 paper may be a little too expensive on the yield curve, analysts said.
They said the only factors overshadowing Thursday's auctions could be recent extreme bullishness on Finnish bonds, which has sent yields tumbling.
"When (bond) yields are at the bottom of their current trading range, income is seen lower and that naturally has a dampening impact on the auction," one dealer said.
"Some state-regulated institutions, for example, have set a six percent yield target (minimum) for their investments," he added, referring to a target premium over current yields.

Finnish bonds have outperformed German Bunds in the past month, spurred by optimism about Finland's expected entry into ERM, and anlysts said Finland's 65 basis point yield premium over Germany could narrow further in the near future.
Enskilda's Pertti Thornberg said the spread, which has narrowed more 35 basis points in the past month, could "easily" tighten below 60 basis points, even before news of a markka-ERM link.
The State Treasury (STO) will take bids for the bonds until 1300/1000 GMT and results are due after 1330/1030 GMT.
